Package hadur2.core.memory

Class Estimate

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.memory.Estimate
public final class Estimate extends Object
A rate and its 95% margin of error (DIAL-1): every input the opening book reads carries both, so a policy can tell "their gun hits 15% of the time" from "it hit 1 of 6 shots".

The margin is Agresti-Coull's: the rate of hits + 2 in n + 4. Unlike the plain Wald interval, it stays wide for a rate of 0 or 1 over few samples. The formula is even defined with no samples at all (about 49%), although of(double, double) returns NONE in that case so that "nothing known" is explicit.

Concretely, with h hits in n trials:

  • value() is the raw rate h / n;
  • center() is p = (h + 2) / (n + 4), the Agresti-Coull centre;
  • margin() is 1.96 * sqrt(p (1 - p) / (n + 4)), the half-width of the 95% interval around that centre (1.96 is the normal distribution's 97.5th percentile).

Hits may be weighted (a normalised hit counts for less than 1), so h and n are doubles. Rates, centres and margins are all fractions in [0, 1], not percentages: a margin of 0.03 is 3 points.

Instances are immutable. The adapt package reads tiers from them (Tiers), RES-4's seed trust compares live estimates with the profile's, and the S5 and S6 policies in hadur2.core.policy compare centres and margins (DIST-1, POW-2, MOVE-2).

    • center

      public double center()
      The centre the margin is measured from: Agresti-Coull's rate of hits + 2 in n + 4, pulled toward a half when there are few samples. A bound that must hold with 95% confidence is center() +- margin(); the raw value can sit at 0 or 1, right at the edge of an interval that is not centred on it. NaN when nothing is known.
      Returns:
      the Agresti-Coull centre, a fraction in [0, 1], or NaN

    • within

      public boolean within(double threshold)
      Whether the margin is at most threshold: a policy may act on it (DIAL-1).
      Parameters:
      threshold - the widest margin the policy accepts, as a fraction
      Returns:
      false for NONE, whatever the threshold

    • excludes

      public boolean excludes(double other)
      Whether other lies outside this estimate's margin (RES-4).

      Measured from the raw value(), not the centre. The main code's seed trust (hadur2.core.adapt.SeedTrust) makes its own comparison; this method is used by the tests.

      Parameters:
      other - a rate to test, as a fraction
      Returns:
      false when either side is unknown
